newsitem.title: UK: Green stg to revalue, four others devalue - HGCA.
newsitem.headline: Green stg to revalue, four others devalue - HGCA.

text.p: The green rate of sterling will revalue in the European Union's agrimonetary grid on Friday, reflecting the currency's recent strength, the UK"s Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Thursday.
At the same time, the green rates of the mark, schilling, guilder and Belgian franc would be devalued, it said.
The HGCA calculated the new green rate for sterling, which underwent a single confirmation period, as 0.809915 per Ecu from the previous 0.833821.
The green mark would devalue to 1.92441 per Ecu from 1.92391, schilling to 13.5396 from 13.5355, the Belgian franc to 39.6411 from 39.6374 and the guilder to 2.15852 from 2.15840.
The spate of devaluations followed the strength of the Irish punt in farm grid as it was entering its fifth and last 10-day confirmation period on Friday for a possible revaluation.
All green currencies trading above their market rates are brought down to level at the end of each confirmation period when at least one currency is assessed for a revaluation.
Green rates are used for European farm subsidy payments.
